Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

dnsr 0.7.0

One-step state-space estimation

estimate_dns_state_space() fits the DNS model by maximum likelihood with a Kalman filter, treating the factors as an unobserved state rather than fitting them curve by curve and then modelling them. This is the state-space form of Diebold, Rudebusch and Aruoba (2006), as against the two-step approach of Diebold and Li (2006) that fit_dns_model() and estimate_dns_dynamics() implement.

The two-step estimator uses the fitted betas as data. They are estimates carrying sampling error, and using them as observed biases mean reversion upward. Filtering the factors propagates that uncertainty into the likelihood and estimates lambda jointly with the dynamics.

The factor system is parameterised in continuous time, with the transition matrices derived from the exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck law rather than estimated freely. The covariance is then positive semi-definite at every trial point, kappa > 0 makes the system stationary, and the result is accepted by dns_dynamics_to_sim_params() without conversion. The cost is that cross-factor terms cannot be represented; use estimate_dns_dynamics(structure = "full") on two-step betas for those.

The result carries smoothed and filtered factors, measurement error by maturity, the log-likelihood with AIC and BIC, and the two-step estimates used as starting values. print() and summary() methods report them.

On the precision of the estimates, measured by simulating from a known state space and re-estimating: lambda, the shock volatilities and the measurement error are recovered to within 1 to 5 percent at 20, 40 and 100 years of monthly data, and the smoothed factors correlate above 0.99 with the simulated ones. The mean reversion speeds and long-run means are not: kappa for the level factor is 167 percent too high at 20 years, 77 percent at 40 and 58 percent at 100. The errors shrink as the sample grows, so this reflects the difficulty of estimating mean reversion rather than an error in the implementation, and it applies to the two-step route as well. ?estimate_dns_state_space gives the full comparison.

Documentation

Rhetorical phrasing removed from the documentation, comments and vignettes in favour of plain statements. The introduction vignette gains a section on one-step estimation and no longer lists the Kalman filter as absent.

dnsr 0.6.0

The lambda search, and the default it starts from. Every function keeps its signature, its return structure and its class; the numbers move, because the old ones came from a search that was not searching and a default that placed the curvature hump past the end of most curves. Passing initial_lambda = 0.0609, method = "optim" reproduces the previous results.

The cross-sectional search now actually searches

fit_ns_model() minimised a sum of squared errors of about 1e-5. L-BFGS-B stops when the reduction in the objective, divided by max(|f|, 1), falls below factr * .Machine$double.eps; with an objective that small the denominator is the constant 1, so the relative test became an absolute one of roughly 2.2e-9 and the search reported success after as few as 17 function evaluations, having barely moved off its start value.

The objective is now minimised in squared basis points, which puts it above 1 where that test measures what it is documented to measure. A positive constant does not move the minimiser, so the reported parameters are those of the same problem; only the stopping decision changes. On the bundled panel, mean fit error over 120 sampled dates:

before after
initial_lambda = 0.0609 10.308 bp 9.715 bp
initial_lambda = 0.5124 9.617 bp 8.620 bp

Two consequences. Warm starting in fit_dns_model() now changes speed rather than answers, because both chains reach the same optimum. And a search that moves can reach the degenerate small-lambda corner, where the level and slope loadings both tend to 1, the design goes collinear and the curvature factor runs to its bound; from the old 0.0609 default that happened on 6 of 72 month-ends. The next section is why.

fit_ns_model() also gained a control argument, forwarded to optim(). It is appended to the signature, so positional calls are unaffected.

The default lambda, and the range it is searched over

lambda is per unit of maturity, and every function here takes maturities in years. The old default of 0.0609 is the value Diebold and Li published for maturities in months: in years it places the curvature hump at 29.4 years, off the end of most curves, where the slope loading is nearly parallel to the level loading and the level and slope factors are not separately identified.

Every lambda default in the package is now ns_lambda(3.5), which places the hump at 3.5 years, near the middle of a Treasury curve. It is written that way so the number states its own meaning. On the bundled panel, fitting a single fixed lambda to all 1,501 curves:

0.0609 ns_lambda(3.5)
panel fit error 20.69 bp 11.81 bp
median day-to-day change in beta1 17.92 bp 3.55 bp
median day-to-day change in beta2 18.11 bp 3.88 bp
median day-to-day change in beta3 37.21 bp 8.61 bp
largest beta3 2386 bp 491 bp

The factor columns are the more consequential ones: at 0.0609 the factors were five times noisier day to day and beta3 reached 23.9 percentage points, because two of the three were not separately identified and moved in offsetting directions. The package estimates the dynamics of those factors.

The ceiling on lambda rises from 0.5 to 2. At 0.5 it bound roughly a third of real month-end curves, and raising the default start made that worse before it made it better. Fitting the 72 month-ends in the bundled panel:

median fit error fits resting on a bound
old default, old ceiling 6.051 bp 25 of 71
new default, old ceiling 4.685 bp 29 of 72
new default, new ceiling 4.467 bp 9 of 72

A clamped lambda is reported through at_bound. The ceiling is 2 rather than higher because lambda is a shape parameter: factors estimated at different lambda are not on the same scale, so a looser ceiling lowers in-sample error at the cost of comparability across dates, which the dynamics step requires.

method = “profile” searches lambda globally

The profiled objective is not unimodal: a basin near zero, where both the level and slope loadings tend to 1, is separated from the basin a real curve wants by a ridge. optimize() is a local bracketing search, so it returned whichever basin its first three probes happened to straddle. Widening the interval to the new ceiling made this visible – it began missing the optimum of a curve that is exactly Nelson-Siegel, with a known answer.

method = "profile" now scans a log-spaced grid over the lambda interval and refines between the neighbouring grid points, which bracket the minimum. The scan is log-spaced because lambda acts as a reciprocal maturity: 0.02 to 0.04 moves the hump 45 years, 1.00 to 1.02 moves it half a month. On an exactly representable curve it recovers lambda to six decimals and fits to 1e-12.

…and is now the default

With the grid in place, profiling is better than optim on every axis measured over 200 curves from the bundled panel, so it becomes the default method for fit_ns_model() and fit_dns_model():

starting lambda optim profile
0.0609 8.516 bp 5.566 bp
ns_lambda(3.5) 5.741 bp 5.566 bp
1.5 5.966 bp 5.566 bp

Profiling is exactly independent of the starting value, a spread of 0.000 bp against 2.775; takes about a third of the time; and had no convergence failures where optim had three. The two agree on the typical curve – median difference in lambda of 1e-5 – and where they disagree by more than 0.05, which is 15 of the 200, the profiled fit is the better of the two on all 15.

method = "optim" remains available and is unchanged apart from the scaled objective. Pass it to reproduce a fit made with an earlier version. One behavioural difference worth knowing: profiling solves the betas by unconstrained least squares, so it does not consult lower_bounds and upper_bounds for the betas and cannot return a beta resting on one. Only lambda is bounded under profiling.

The model comparison no longer understates Nelson-Siegel

compare_term_structure_models() fits the Nelson-Siegel row with fit_ns_model(), so it inherited both defects above. On the bundled panel it reported 8.87 bp for Nelson-Siegel, behind the cubic spline’s 5.56; it now reports 4.43, ahead of it. The comparison itself is unchanged; the row was being fitted with a poor lambda and a weak search.

It gains initial_lambda and method, forwarded to fit_ns_model() and appended to the signature, so the row is reproducible rather than merely better. The other rows take no search and are unaffected.

Documentation that the above made wrong

The introduction vignette asserted that the default lambda ceiling of 0.5 was binding on the latest curve, and printed an at_bound report to prove it. With the ceiling at 2 nothing is clamped, so that section now imposes the old ceiling explicitly to show what a clamped fit looks like – lambda resting on 0.5 at 4.95 bp against 4.43 unclamped – which makes the same point without depending on a defect. The free-lambda range quoted for the panel (0.04 to 0.50) and the cost of fixing lambda (14 bp against 7) are both remeasured: 0.17 to 2.00, and 6.4 bp against 4.5.

The table comparing lambda = 0.0609 with 0.448 is unchanged, because it passes both values explicitly; two rounded entries are corrected to the measured 29.4 years and -0.928. The README no longer says 0.0609 “remains this package’s default for continuity”, and the YUIMA vignette passes ns_lambda(3.5) rather than 0.0609 in its three simulation calls.

dnsr 0.5.0

Documentation, plus one additive pair of helpers. No existing function changes what it computes.

The lambda units, and why they matter more than they look

lambda is measured per unit of maturity, and every function here takes maturities in years. The 0.0609 default is the value Diebold and Li published for maturities in months, where it places the curvature hump just short of 30 months. In years the same number places it at 29.4 – off the end of most curves.

That was documented nowhere, and the consequence is larger than a misplaced hump. At lambda = 0.0609 the slope loading falls only from 0.992 at three months to 0.749 at ten years: nearly flat, and so nearly collinear with the level loading, which is 1 everywhere. The two factors stop being separately identified. Fitting the bundled panel both ways and comparing beta2 against the 3-month minus 10-year spread the market quotes:

lambda hump at cor(beta2, 3m-10y) same sign median fit
0.0609 29.5 y -0.929 5% 23.0 bp
0.448 4.0 y +0.941 90% 5.3 bp

At the default the slope factor is anti-correlated with the slope and carries the right sign on one date in twenty.

The default is unchanged, because changing it would alter every existing call, and because there is no single right value to substitute: 0.73 reproduces the Diebold-Li criterion in year units, while this panel prefers about 0.45. What changes is that the units are now stated wherever lambda is documented, and there is a way to reason about it:

  • New ns_lambda() and ns_curvature_peak() convert between a decay and the maturity at which its curvature loading peaks, which is the quantity a reader can actually judge. ns_lambda(2.5) describes the same curve shape whether maturities are years or months, because the caller states the maturity in their own units. ns_curvature_peak(0.0609) reports 29.4, which is how the mismatch becomes visible.

    Documented with its two caveats: the peak is flat, so lambda is not tightly determined by this choice, and lambda sets the slope loading’s decay at the same time, which is often the more consequential effect.

  • fit_ns_model()’s documentation now says that with method = "optim" the search over lambda is weak – L-BFGS-B’s numerical gradient is poorly scaled when the betas are near 0.05 and lambda near 0.5, and lambda moves very little from its starting value even unconstrained – while method = "profile" searches it properly and reaches the same optimum from any start.

Vignettes

  • The introduction now explains the lambda units with the measurement above, fixes lambda at ns_lambda(4) for its panel work rather than at the default, and gains three sections: whether the factors mean what they are called (beta2 against the quoted spread), where a three-factor curve runs out (residuals by maturity, from 1.9 basis points in the middle to 9.4 at the long end, with twenty years fitted low and thirty high), and a checklist for deciding whether a fit is trustworthy that gathers success_rate, failures, at_bound, system_stability and half_life_ci into one place.
  • A section on what the package does not do: it estimates in two steps rather than as a state-space system with a Kalman filter, so the standard errors describe the factor regressions and not the factors’ own measurement error; and it carries no arbitrage-free restriction, which matters if curves are being used to price derivatives rather than discount cashflows.
  • README.md tabulates the whole exported surface, not just the plots. dns_zero_prices() had appeared nowhere in it.

Removed

  • dnsr-package-summary.Rmd, which carried vignette metadata but sat in the repository root, was .Rbuildignored, and was therefore never built, shipped or checked. It duplicated README.md and had rotted unnoticed – it still documented animate_yield_curves(), removed long ago, and listed none of the functions added since. The only thing referencing it was a stale local docs/ build.

dnsr 0.4.3

  • fit_dns_model() gains lower_bounds and upper_bounds, forwarded to fit_ns_model(). The panel fitter reports clamped fits in at_bound and warns about them, but had no argument through which to do anything about it: widening the box meant abandoning fit_dns_model() and looping fit_ns_model() by hand. On the bundled treasury_yields month-ends a freely estimated lambda rests on its default ceiling of 0.5 on 13 of 72 dates; passing wider bounds clears all 13 and improves the median fit.

    Both default to NULL rather than to fit_ns_model()’s own numeric defaults, and are forwarded only when supplied. That is deliberate: fit_ns_model() decides whether to widen its beta box to the data scale by asking whether both bounds are missing(), so passing its defaults through explicitly would have switched that off and reintroduced the clamping on percentage-point yields that 0.4.0 fixed. Both behaviours are tested.

dnsr 0.4.2

The vignettes, which had been left at 0.1.0-era content while everything else moved, plus one defect they surfaced.

Fix

  • estimate_dns_dynamics(structure = "full") warned “No mean reversion detected” whenever a factor’s own diagonal entry came out non-positive. That is the right diagnostic for the diagonal structure, where a non-positive kappa does mean the factor never reverts, and the wrong one for a full matrix, where a negative own coefficient is perfectly compatible with a stable system: what settles that is the eigenvalues of the whole matrix. On the bundled panel the full VAR has kappa[1,1] = -2.6 and eigenvalues of 1.40, 1.40 and 0.49 – stable, and warned about anyway. The per-factor warning is now raised only under structure = "diagonal", and a system whose eigenvalues are not all positive raises one warning naming them.

Vignettes

  • dns-model-introduction ran almost nothing: 14 of its 16 chunks were eval = FALSE, and the two that ran fabricated yields with rnorm(). It now runs end to end against the bundled treasury_yields panel, so the output is real and R CMD check verifies it. It covers the profiled fit, print() and summary(), the standard errors and half-life interval, the full mean-reversion matrix, the exact simulation engine, the pricing helpers, and the model comparison.

    It also now explains the choice a panel forces and a single curve does not: with lambda free it ranges from 0.04 to 0.50 across these dates, so beta2 on one date does not mean what it means on the next and the factors stop being a comparable time series. Fixing lambda, as Diebold and Li do, costs about 14 basis points of median fit against 7 and buys factors that can be modelled over time.

  • dnsr-yuima-integration claimed "milstein" gives “higher accuracy”. It does not: the Milstein correction is proportional to the derivative of the diffusion with respect to the state, and this diffusion is constant, so the term vanishes and the two schemes coincide. Removed, and the two engines now have a section explaining what each is actually for.

    Its 41-line hand-rolled Euler fallback for when YUIMA is absent is gone; engine = "exact" does that properly, with no discretisation error.

    The QMLE section printed a true-versus-estimated table with no comment, and the table is alarming on its face: kappa for the level factor comes back 120 times too large. The vignette now explains why, which makes it the most useful passage in it. Sigma is recovered to within a few percent, because volatility is identified by high-frequency variation. Kappa is not, and the error tracks the ratio of each factor’s half-life to the sample: 35 years against 2 gives 120x, 2.3 years gives 7x, 1.4 years gives 1.3x. No estimator recovers a 35-year half-life from two years of data, and theta inherits the problem, since the level a process reverts to is identified only if the reversion is.

  • fred-api-setup told readers to hand-roll a caching layer and to wait out rate limits. Both are built in now, so it documents cache_dir and retries instead – including that cache keys exclude the API key, that a hit is served before the key is looked up, and that the cache does not expire. It gains a section on missing observations covering max_gap, fill_missing and why the fill direction matters, a note on date_order, and a pointer to the bundled data for readers who do not need a key yet.

  • Fixed a broken cross-reference: the introduction pointed at vignette("yuima-integration"), which does not exist.

dnsr 0.4.1

Follow-ups to 0.4.0: no change to what any function computes, except one documentation correction.

  • fit_dns_model()’s warm start makes a date’s fit depend on which other dates are in the panel, because each cross-section is initialised from the previous date’s lambda and the chain differs. Fitting a month-end series directly and fitting the daily series containing it give lambdas differing by up to 0.096 on the shared dates. That is inherent to warm starting rather than a defect, but it was undocumented, and warm_start = FALSE makes the fits panel-independent – verified identical, not merely close. Now documented, and pinned by a test.
  • The estimate_dns_dynamics() and dns_dynamics_to_sim_params() examples fitted 750 cross-sections to reach the 20 month-ends the default monthly sampling needs, taking about 9 seconds each and tripping the CRAN check note for examples over 5 seconds. They now fit only the month-ends the estimation actually uses, with warm_start = FALSE so the result matches what fitting every day would give. About nine times quicker.
  • Offline coverage for the FRED data path, which the live tests skip and which was the least-covered file at 22.7 percent. Two routes, neither needing a key or a network: a prepared cache, which fetch_fred_series() consults before looking for a key, so the whole assembly in get_treasury_yield_data() runs for real; and mockery for the request and parse layer the cache skips. Covers the “.” to NA mapping, HTTP failure reporting, the empty-payload warning, the cache round trip including that no key reaches disk, decimal conversion, row ordering, gap filling with max_gap, and per-series fetch failures. R/data-utils.r goes from 22.7 to 92.8 percent and the package from 76.2 to 82.4.
  • Trimmed the test suite from 73 to 40 seconds without weakening an assertion: the exact simulation engine is exact at any step size, so the stationary test uses 120 steps rather than 720; the transition-law test needs fewer paths than it had, since its assertions are z-scores against the Monte Carlo standard error; the plan-restoration test uses a tweaked sequential plan, which is distinguishable from the plain one the bug installed and needs no workers; and the Svensson sweep uses a wider stride over the same range. The coverage job was taking 17 minutes.
  • New pkgdown workflow. _pkgdown.yml arrived in 0.4.0 but nothing rendered it: docs/ was a gitignored local build, never committed, ten months stale, documenting three functions that no longer existed and missing six that did. The site is now built on a runner that has pandoc and published to gh-pages. Standing the workflow up immediately showed the index was incomplete – it omitted the dnsr-package topic, which pkgdown treats as an error – a gap that had gone unnoticed because nothing had ever rendered the config.

dnsr 0.4.0

Enhancements, all reachable only through new arguments and new exports, plus one correctness fix in the factor dynamics. Nothing that existed before changes its name, arguments or argument order.

Correctness

  • estimate_dns_dynamics() regressed the factor change on the contemporaneous level rather than the lagged level its own documented model specifies. Since beta(t) appears on both sides of beta(t) - beta(t-1), the ordinary least squares slope came back with the opposite sign: +(1 - phi) instead of -(1 - phi). The consequences were systematic rather than occasional:
    • kappa was computed negative for every factor on every call, and the kappa <= 0 guard then rescued it with abs(), which recovers roughly the right magnitude and so hid the problem.
    • because that guard always fired, theta always fell back to the sample mean, and the documented -a/b estimator never once executed.
    • system_stability was always TRUE, since abs() forced kappa positive.
    The regression is now on beta(t-1), derived as the level minus the change so it is exact under either sampling mode. kappa comes out positive on its own, theta comes from the intercept and slope, and a genuinely non-reverting factor now raises a warning naming the factor instead of being silently turned around. On the bundled Treasury panel this moves kappa by about 0.1 percent and leaves theta unchanged, because the two slopes are mirror images; it is decisive for the full mean-reversion matrix below, where there is no scalar sign for abs() to flip.

New capabilities

  • fit_ns_model() and fit_dns_model() gain method. method = "profile" concentrates the sum of squared errors: with lambda fixed the curve is linear in the betas, so they are solved exactly by least squares and only lambda is searched, over one dimension. It needs no start values, consults no beta bounds, and cannot return a clamped beta. On a synthetic Nelson-Siegel curve it recovers lambda to five decimals where the numerical search reaches three. "optim" remains the default.

  • estimate_dns_dynamics() gains structure = "full", which regresses each factor change on all three lagged levels and returns the full mean-reversion matrix of the Diebold-Li VAR(1) in kappa_matrix, with long-run means solved from it in theta_vector. kappa_matrix_eigenvalues() now uses that matrix, so the stability verdict accounts for the cross terms. "diagonal" remains the default and still produces a diagonal kappa_matrix.

  • Each factor’s dynamics now carry se (standard errors of kappa, theta and sigma), t_value and half_life_ci. kappa’s standard error rescales from the slope’s; theta’s comes from the delta method, since it is a ratio of coefficients. These describe sampling noise, not the upward small-sample bias in kappa, which is documented separately.

  • New dns_discount_factors(), dns_zero_prices() and dns_par_yields() convert factors into the quantities a cashflow valuation consumes. Par yields are computed on the annuity factor and are defined only on whole numbers of coupon periods; shorter maturities return NA with a warning rather than being forced onto a convention they do not have.

  • New treasury_yields dataset: 1,501 daily curves across eleven maturities, 2019 to 2024, from FRED’s H.15 Treasury constant maturity series. Six years spans 72 month-ends, enough for the default monthly dynamics estimation. Most examples now run against it instead of sitting inside \dontrun{}, and the test suite can cover the data path offline. Built by data-raw/treasury_yields.R.

  • fetch_fred_series() and get_treasury_yield_data() gain retries and cache_dir. Requests are retried with exponential backoff on transient failures but not on a 4xx, where retrying cannot help. Cache keys cover the series and date range only: the API key is never part of the key and never written to disk, and a cache hit is served before the key is looked up, so a cached corpus can be replayed with no key configured.

  • fit_ns_model(), fit_dns_model(), estimate_dns_dynamics() and the two simulators now return classed objects with print() methods, and fit_dns_model() also has summary(). These are classes layered onto the lists already returned: every element keeps its name, and is.list(), $ and checkmate::assert_list() behave as before. Only the default display changes.

  • The Nelson-Siegel-Svensson comparison in compare_term_structure_models() could never have produced a column. It called SmithWilson::Nelson.Siegel.Svensson(), and SmithWilson is not a package: the one that exists is SmithWilsonYieldCurve. So requireNamespace("SmithWilson") returned FALSE on every machine and the branch always skipped with a warning. Correcting the name would not have helped either, because SmithWilsonYieldCurve exports only fFitSmithWilsonYieldCurve() and fFitSmithWilsonYieldCurveToInstruments() – no Svensson fitter.

    Svensson is now fitted directly. The curve is linear in its four betas once the two decays are fixed, so it uses the same concentrated least squares as method = "profile", with the decays searched over a coarse grid and then refined. The comparison is therefore available to everyone with no optional dependency, both decays are estimated rather than fixed at 0.5 and 3, and on the bundled panel it fits better than Nelson-Siegel on every date, as a nested model must.

    The search is bounded because the profiled residual has three degenerate corners that fit beautifully and mean nothing: the two decays coinciding, the first approaching zero (the slope loading flattens to a constant and goes collinear with the intercept), and the first growing large (every loading but the level decays to nothing inside the shortest maturity). Unbounded, the search returned lambda1 = 1e-4 with betas of plus and minus 16,800 on one real date. Bounded, no date in the panel produces a factor above 1 in magnitude.

  • New "SmithWilson" option in compare_term_structure_models(), which is what SmithWilsonYieldCurve actually provides, with ufr and alpha arguments. It is opt-in rather than in the default models, and documented as an interpolation rather than a fit: it carries one kernel term per instrument, so it reproduces every observed yield to within 4e-12 basis points and its error metrics are zero by construction, not comparable with a three- or four-factor curve’s. The useful part is its extrapolation beyond the last maturity, which converges to ufr.

  • Dropped gganimate and gifski from Suggests; nothing has referenced them since animate_yield_curves() was removed.

  • plot_yield_pca() gains scale. scale = FALSE decomposes the covariance matrix rather than standardising each maturity first, which is the usual convention for yield curves and is what produces the familiar level, slope and curvature shapes. TRUE remains the default.

Other fixes

  • fit_dns_model() reports parameters resting on a bound once for the whole panel, naming each parameter and the number of dates, instead of emitting one warning per date; a run over several hundred dates could previously produce hundreds. The per-date detail is in the new at_bound element, a logical matrix kept beside parameters rather than inside it, so that frame stays numeric apart from its Date column.
  • The Greek letters in plot labels made several plots unrenderable on Windows. The default device there converts text through a single-byte charset and fails outright on U+03BB: conversion failure on 'lambda = 0.0609' in 'mbcsToSbcs'. plot_dns_loadings() and plot_factor_time_series() now use plotmath, which goes through R’s symbol font and renders anywhere, and the package source is fully ASCII. The bug predates this release; it surfaced only once the examples became runnable and R CMD check started drawing them. A test now prints every plot to a null device, since ggplot_build() stops short of text measurement and cannot catch this class of fault.
  • geom_line(size = ) replaced with linewidth =, which ggplot2 has wanted since 3.4.
  • plot_yield_heatmap() decided whether to rescale yields to percent one column at a time, so a panel whose short end was below 1 and long end above it could be drawn in two different units. The decision is now made once from the whole frame. plot_type = "curvature" with fewer than three maturities counted backwards through its loop and now reports the requirement.
  • dns_to_yuima_model() tested the correlation diagonal for exact equality with 1, rejecting matrices that are correct to within rounding.
  • The package-level example simulated from dynamics$initial_factors, which estimate_dns_dynamics() has never returned, so it errored. It now starts from the most recent fitted factors.
  • The internal Nelson-Siegel loading formula had four copies; it is now defined once. The arithmetic is unchanged, so yields and forwards remain identical to the last bit.
  • Dropped an unused local in plot_simulated_factors().

dnsr 0.3.0

Correctness, performance and packaging release. Every exported function keeps its name, arguments and argument order; new behaviour is reachable only through new trailing arguments whose defaults reproduce 0.2.0. Four returned values change, each because the old value was wrong — see Values that change below.

Critical fixes

  • get_treasury_yield_data() filled missing yields backwards in calendar time. The frame is sorted most-recent-first and the fill ran in row order, so each gap took the value of the next later date — look-ahead bias, on by default, in every panel with holes (DGS20 before 1993, DGS30 between 2002 and 2006). Gap filling now runs on an ascending date index. New max_gap caps how many calendar days a value may be carried, and new date_order chooses the row order of the result.
  • fit_dns_model() selected the oldest n_days rows, not the most recent. It took the last rows of the frame, which is only “most recent” for ascending input, while this package’s own data functions return descending. The window is now chosen by date and does not depend on row order. New date_order controls the output order and defaults to "input", so parameters[1, ] remains the most recent row for a most-recent-first frame.
  • Cross-sections that could not be fitted survived as zero-factor rows. params_df was pre-allocated with numeric(), so failed dates kept beta1 = beta2 = beta3 = rmse = 0 and the !is.na(beta1) filter meant to drop them never matched. Failed dates are now NA and are removed; new drop_failed = FALSE keeps them as NA, and the result gains a failures data frame naming each date and reason.
  • A single missing maturity on a single date aborted the whole fit with number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length. fit_ns_model() returns fitted values only for the maturities it retained; these are now placed back into a full-width row by index, leaving absent maturities as NA. fit_ns_model() gains valid_idx for this purpose.
  • beta*_change columns were differenced in row order rather than calendar order, so for descending input every change had the wrong sign and the change-on-level slope — and therefore kappa — flipped. Changes are now first differences in calendar order, written back in the output’s row order.
  • fit_dns_model(parallel = FALSE) permanently reset the caller’s future::plan() to sequential, tearing down a multisession pool set up for the rest of the session. No plan is now changed as a side effect, and the parallel = TRUE path restores the previous plan on exit.
  • The lambda warm start was carried in last_fit_result <<- result, which wrote into the global environment and could not work under future_lapply() in any case. Warm starting is now explicit, local, and walks forward in calendar time; new warm_start = FALSE disables it.

Other fixes

  • compare_term_structure_models() scaled its error metrics by 100 while labelling them basis points — every reported RMSE, MAE and MaxError was 100x too small. Decimal yields now scale by 10,000, matching fit_dns_model(). New units = "decimal" returns them in the units of the input. The function also no longer breaks on a maturity with no observation on the chosen date.
  • simulate_dns_yield_curves() validated sim_method and then discarded it, so "milstein" silently ran Euler. simulate_dns_factors() gains sim_method and the value is forwarded and recorded on the result. (For this model the diffusion is state-independent, so the two schemes coincide; the documentation now says so.)
  • plot_yield_curves() labelled facets with integer date codes (“19369”): intersect() and for (date in dates) both drop the Date class. Facets are now dated and ordered by calendar. RMSE annotations moved to their own layer instead of being smuggled through the colour scale as a fake series.
  • plot_simulated_factors() failed on a single-path simulation (dim(X) must have a positive length), as did the term-structure branch of plot_simulated_yields(). Both now keep the path dimension.
  • plot_yield_heatmap(reverse_time = TRUE) was a no-op, and its documentation described the default orientation rather than the effect of setting it: a date axis increases upward, so the most recent date was already at the top. The argument now flips the axis, putting the most recent date at the bottom, and says so. It is implemented on the data rather than through the scale or the coordinate system, because neither is portable – scale_y_reverse() negates the variable and unary minus is undefined for Date, while coord_cartesian(ylim = rev(range)) reverses the panel on ggplot2 3.x but is normalised away on 4.x.
  • plot_yield_pca() errored with object 'var_explained' not found when all three plot_* flags were FALSE.
  • plot_simulated_yields() facets sorted lexically, putting “Year 10” between “Year 1” and “Year 5” for the default time_points.
  • dns_dynamics_to_sim_params() always returned lambda = 0.0609; the branch meant to override it could never fire, because estimate_dns_dynamics() does not return a lambda. New lambda argument, and get_calibrated_dns_params() now passes the lambda it actually fitted.
  • fit_ns_model()’s default bounds assumed decimal yields and clamped silently. L-BFGS-B reports convergence == 0 at a bound, so a clamped fit was returned with success = TRUE: percentage-point yields pinned all four parameters at their bounds with an RMSE of 2.7 percentage points. Default beta bounds now widen to cover the data scale, start values are kept inside the box, and any parameter resting on a bound is reported in the new at_bound field and raises a warning. An explicitly supplied optimizer is now honoured by lambda_constraint = "free", which previously always used BFGS. The slope start value is taken by maturity rather than by position.
  • estimate_dns_parameters_yuima() took factor columns positionally, so passing the parameters frame the documentation describes fed Date into diff(). Columns named beta1/beta2/beta3 are now used when present.
  • get_calibrated_dns_params() gains api_key; the calibration path was previously reachable only through the environment variable. Its “latest” factors and lambda are now selected by date rather than by row position.
  • tests/testthat.R was missing, so R CMD check skipped the entire test suite. Added, along with mockery in Suggests and a regression test for each fix above.

Performance

  • calculate_dns_yields() and calculate_dns_forwards() were triple loops over scalars. Only the maturity dimension is looped now; time and path are handled by vectorised arithmetic, with the expression and its left-to-right grouping unchanged, so results are identical to the last bit. On 601 steps x 500 paths x 11 maturities: yields 24.0s to 0.079s, forwards 2.33s to 0.089s. (The gap between the two was loadings[m_idx, "loading_2"] – indexing a matrix by column name inside the innermost loop.)
  • New engine argument on simulate_dns_factors() and simulate_dns_yield_curves(). engine = "exact" samples the factor system’s exact Gaussian transition law instead of calling yuima::simulate() once per path: no discretisation error at any step size, no YUIMA dependency, and about 120x faster (100 paths x 120 steps: 1.78s to 0.015s). The step covariance is built as rho_ij sigma_i sigma_j (1 - exp(-(kappa_i + kappa_j) dt)) / (kappa_i + kappa_j), which couples the two reversion speeds – using each factor’s own variance with a Cholesky factor of the correlation matrix is only correct when every kappa is equal. The default remains "yuima"; the two engines agree in distribution but do not produce the same paths from the same seed. The default is expected to change to "exact" in a future release.
  • fit_dns_model() no longer searches for each date’s row with which(Date == date), which made the fit quadratic in the number of dates.
  • The plot_simulated_factors() and plot_simulated_yields() frames are built in one pass instead of by rbind() inside nested loops. Row order and values are unchanged.

Package health

R CMD check went from 4 warnings and 4 notes to zero of either, with the test suite running for the first time. Remaining output on a given machine is limited to uninstalled Suggests packages and, where pandoc is absent, unbuilt vignettes.

  • R/dnsr-package.R was at the repository root as dnsr-package.r, so its roxygen block never ran and the file was never sourced: the package-level help page and its @import directives were both dead. Moved into R/, and ?dnsr-package now exists. dnsr-structure.txt and dnsr-package-summary.Rmd are no longer shipped in the tarball.
  • Non-ASCII characters removed from R/: the Greek letters and subscripts in plot labels are now \uxxxx escapes, which renders identically, and the mathematical notation in comments is plain ASCII.
  • LICENSE is now the two-field DCF stub that MIT + file LICENSE requires; the full text moved to LICENSE.note, which still ships.
  • Added the missing importFrom(stats, ...) entries for cor, median and residuals, and a utils::globalVariables() registration for the columns created inside functions and then referenced in ggplot2 aesthetics. The “no visible binding” and “no visible global function definition” notes – 40 of them – are gone.
  • Dropped readr, data.table, Matrix, tidyr and lubridate from Imports: nothing in the package referenced them. The dplyr verb imports were also unused; only the pipe is kept, for plot_yield_surface().
  • [time, path, factor] in @return and @param text was being parsed as an Rd link, producing cross-reference warnings. Rewritten as prose.
  • The YUIMA vignette could not be built on a machine without YUIMA: has_yuima was defined inside a chunk gated on eval = requireNamespace( "yuima"), so when that was FALSE the chunk never ran and the fallback chunks testing eval = !has_yuima died with object 'has_yuima' not found. It is now set in the always-run setup chunk.
  • DESCRIPTION gains URL, BugReports, Language and Depends: R (>= 4.1).
  • Added _pkgdown.yml, giving the reference index an organised structure rather than one flat alphabetical list, and GitHub Actions workflows for R CMD check (Linux/macOS/Windows, release and oldrel) and test coverage. There was no CI before, which is how a missing tests/testthat.R went unnoticed.

Values that change

  • Fill direction. Gaps are filled from the last earlier observation rather than the next later one. Opt out with fill_missing = FALSE.
  • Change sign. beta*_change is always beta(t) - beta(t-1). This reaches only callers using estimate_dns_dynamics(sampling = "daily"); the monthly default already recomputed the changes on a sorted grid.
  • Error units. compare_term_structure_models()$metrics is now genuinely in basis points, so the values are 100x their 0.2.0 counterparts. Pass units = "decimal" for the input’s own units.
  • Simulation lambda. get_calibrated_dns_params()$params$lambda is the fitted lambda rather than a hard-coded 0.0609. dns_dynamics_to_sim_params() called directly, with no lambda argument, still returns 0.0609.

Additive changes to returned objects: fit_ns_model() gains valid_idx and at_bound; fit_dns_model() gains failures; simulate_dns_factors() and simulate_dns_yield_curves() gain sim_method and engine. Code reading these lists by name is unaffected; code asserting an exact set of element names is not.

dnsr 0.2.0

estimate_dns_dynamics() owns the sampling policy

  • New sampling argument: "monthly" (the default) subsamples the factor series to its last observation per month, recomputes the change columns on the month-end grid, and estimates at dt = 1/12, per Diebold-Li practice. Daily cross-sectional refits carry serially uncorrelated measurement noise that the OU change-on-level regression reads as mean reversion, inflating kappa by an order of magnitude; month-end sampling averages the noise down and recovers reversion speeds on the economically meaningful time scale. Every caller now gets this policy from one place instead of replicating it.
  • sampling = "daily" estimates on the series as given and reproduces the 0.1.0 behavior exactly (including the dt = 1/252 default).
  • dt now defaults to the sampling mode’s spacing. In monthly mode the step is month-end to month-end by construction, so a conflicting explicit dt is ignored with a warning.
  • Monthly subsampling is idempotent: a series that is already month-end passes through unchanged, so callers that pre-subsample (as get_calibrated_dns_params() did in 0.1.x) get identical estimates.
  • In monthly mode the beta*_change input columns are no longer required; they are derived internally.
  • The returned dynamics gain $innovation_dates (the date axis of the $innovations rows, so consumers can align innovations across models estimated on different calendars), plus $sampling and $dt.
  • get_calibrated_dns_params() now delegates the subsampling to estimate_dns_dynamics(); its results are unchanged.

dnsr 0.1.0

  • Initial release: Treasury data fetch, DNS cross-sectional fitting, OU factor dynamics, simulation, and visualization.
